summary: Retained behavior: a versioned presentation frame contract. Removed concept: the universal RuntimeProjectionFrame schema and authority-tick envelope are split into independently versioned scene and presentation frames.
Removed concept: the enum existed only to label presentation outside replay truth; successor presentation frames omit replay certification entirely.
Removed concept: mandatory authority-origin classification belonged to Asha proof bookkeeping rather than disposable presentation behavior.
Removed concept: mandatory source-fact, authority-tick, causation, and correlation envelopes do not cross the successor render border.
Retained behavior: contiguous per-frame operation sequencing. Removed concept: mandatory authority-origin, causation, and correlation envelopes.
Retained behavior: typed audio failure code, operation sequence, handle, and message. Removed concept: copied authority-origin proof metadata on renderer diagnostics.
Retained behavior: typed billboard failure code, operation sequence, handle, and message. Removed concept: copied authority-origin proof metadata on renderer diagnostics.
Retained behavior: typed particle failure code, operation sequence, handle, and message. Removed concept: copied authority-origin proof metadata on renderer diagnostics.
Retained behavior: typed telemetry failure code, operation sequence, handle, and message. Removed concept: copied authority-origin proof metadata on renderer diagnostics.

Retained behavior: local controller tick, transition identity, endpoints, moment, and duration. Removed concept: source-fact identity, authority tick, input-log sequence, causation, correlation, and certification hash.
Retained behavior: graph version, state revision, resolved motion, active transition, and typed local transition fact. Removed concept: graph and semantic-state certification hashes.
Retained behavior: typed animation failure code, sequence, handle, target, and message. Removed concept: copied authority-origin proof metadata on renderer diagnostics.
Retained behavior: a versioned ordered frame of typed presentation operations. Removed concept: the replay-scope marker that existed only to classify the frame for certification.
Retained behavior: scene and presentation frames can be applied together by an explicit caller. Removed concept: one universal runtime composite carrying authority tick and cross-domain ownership.
Retained behavior: callers can construct empty versioned scene and presentation frames. Removed concept: a RuntimeProjectionFrame constructor that packages them with an authority tick.

Retained behavior: scene and ordered presentation frames remain independently constructible and validated. Removed concept: the runtime composite, authority tick, and replay-exclusion marker asserted by the donor test.
Retained behavior: one controller entity projects to a stable create, update, and destroy handle lifecycle. Removed concept: origin correlation and graph-hash proof fields asserted by the donor test.

Retained behavior: projection rejects a controller state whose entity identity does not match the projected owner. Removed concept: treating that identity check as cross-authority certification rather than local descriptor validation.
Removed concept: rejecting mismatched origin envelopes exists only when the renderer is required to cross-check authority-fact provenance.
Removed concept: canonical catalog, graph, controller-state, replay-log, and stable-id hashes were certification infrastructure rather than animation behavior.
Removed concept: the schema version exists only for the eliminated replay-derived animation authority snapshot format.
Removed concept: the version string identified the old replay-certified animation authority rather than the successor presentation service.
Removed concept: canonical catalog certification hashes are not part of narrow animation catalog validation.

Retained behavior: entity, graph, current state, revision, parameters, motion, transition, and typed local timing fact. Removed concept: graph hash, semantic state hash, and durable gameplay-fact provenance.
Retained behavior: explicit prior revision and optional resulting controller state. Removed concept: previous semantic-state certification hash.
Retained behavior: attach, parameter changes, trigger, and deterministic tick inputs. Removed concept: a mandatory gameplay-fact origin embedded in every tick for later replay.
Removed concept: the input record is solely a durable replay-log entry with a global sequence.
Retained behavior: callers receive the resulting controller change from each explicit operation. Removed concept: replay sequence, semantic state hash, and replay hash receipt fields.
Retained behavior: typed graph, controller, parameter, tick, and corruption failures. Removed concept: snapshot decode, catalog/state/replay mismatch, replay sequence, and origin-proof errors.

Retained behavior: an explicit deterministic service owns presentation-only controller instances. Removed concept: authority naming plus its retained input log, snapshots, hashes, and replay entrypoint.
Removed concept: exposing the controller authority's catalog certification hash served replay and snapshot verification only.
Removed concept: exposing the retained animation input log served verification replay only.
Removed concept: ticking through a mandatory gameplay-fact origin and validating its causation/correlation fields is intentionally outside the presentation controller.
Removed concept: encoding controller state together with its replay log belongs to the eliminated certification snapshot path.
Removed concept: hashing the replay-derived authority snapshot belongs to certification rather than animation behavior.
Removed concept: restoring and verifying animation state from a replay-derived snapshot is intentionally absent.
Removed concept: reconstructing animation authority from retained input records is intentionally absent.
Removed concept: mandatory source-fact, authority-tick, causation, and correlation identity served replay proofing rather than local transition timing.

Retained behavior: a typed local fact reports controller tick, transition endpoints, moment, and duration. Removed concept: durable fact identity, gameplay origin, input sequence, resulting revision proof, and fact hash.

Retained behavior: float, bool, and trigger parameters drive deterministic transition priority, trigger consumption, and linear blend resolution. Removed concept: presenting this disposable controller as gameplay authority with replay-certified state.

Retained behavior: identical explicit controller inputs resolve identical ordinary controller state. Removed concept: retained input records, verification replay, semantic state hashes, and snapshot hashes.
Retained behavior: a deterministic tick emits a typed local transition fact with timing and resolved motion. Removed concept: gameplay-fact provenance retention and verification replay.
Removed concept: entity-independent semantic state hashes existed to compare replay-certified authority states.
Removed concept: the test covers only replay-derived authority snapshot encoding and decoding.
Removed concept: the test covers only snapshot-to-replay-log certification and tamper rejection.

Retained behavior: missing clips, unreachable states, ambiguous transitions, and parameter type mismatches fail admission with typed diagnostics. Removed concept: tying admission to Asha's global catalog-load authority.
Retained behavior: non-positive clip and blend playback speeds fail narrow animation catalog validation. Removed concept: tying this validation to Asha's global catalog-load authority.
Removed concept: canonical catalog hashing existed to bind replay snapshots, while ordinary validation and deterministic transition ordering remain separately evidenced.
Retained behavior: validated states and allowed transition edges back the animation graph. Removed concept: a separate public gameplay-wide finite-state-machine specification owner.
Retained behavior: animation graph admission constructs validated state and transition lookup. Removed concept: publicly constructing a second generic machine specification.
Retained behavior: authored animation transitions declare allowed directed edges. Removed concept: mutating a separate generic machine specification through a builder API.
Retained behavior: animation catalog validation and controller resolution reject unknown states. Removed concept: exposing the generic machine's membership query as public gameplay authority.
Retained behavior: only validated authored animation transitions can be selected. Removed concept: exposing a generic transition-edge query outside the controller owner.
Retained behavior: animation states are stored deterministically for validation and lookup. Removed concept: exposing generic ProcessId and ModeId iteration from a second state owner.
Retained behavior: animation transitions are stored deterministically by source and priority. Removed concept: exposing generic ProcessId and ModeId edge iteration from a second state owner.
Retained behavior: each entity has current animation state and a monotonically advancing revision. Removed concept: a public generic ProcessId and ModeId machine-instance representation.
Removed concept: callers no longer command arbitrary expected-to-next generic state transitions; the animation controller selects validated edges from typed inputs.
Removed concept: constructing an arbitrary generic transition command is absent because controller transitions are condition-selected.
Removed concept: optimistic revision checks on caller-authored generic transition commands are absent with that command surface.

Retained behavior: typed local animation transition facts report state endpoints and revision-related timing. Removed concept: generic machine attach/transition events shared with gameplay process vocabulary.
Removed concept: stable string event-kind labels for the generic machine event and replay vocabulary are not part of local typed animation facts.
Removed concept: formatting machine events as deterministic replay evidence lines is intentionally absent.
Retained behavior: successful animation operations return changed state and a typed transition fact. Removed concept: the generic transition receipt carrying a replay-shaped StateMachineEvent.

Retained behavior: transition selection validates state edges and updates state atomically inside the animation controller. Removed concept: a detached public generic transition primitive driven by arbitrary requests.
Removed concept: bridging generic machine state into Asha's global DomainEvent ProcessModeSet vocabulary is intentionally absent.

Retained behavior: typed graph, state, controller, parameter, and tick failures remain local to the animation service. Removed concept: entity-registry, generic machine-store, global ErrorCategory, and external transition-command variants.
Removed concept: mapping generic machine failures into Asha's global ErrorCategory vocabulary is intentionally absent.
Removed concept: string error codes for the removed generic state-machine command surface are intentionally absent.

Retained behavior: the animation service owns deterministic per-entity controller instances and validated graphs. Removed concept: a second generic gameplay state store with its own entity registry and machine catalog.
Retained behavior: callers construct an explicit animation controller service from a validated catalog. Removed concept: constructing an empty generic state-machine authority store.
Removed concept: presentation code does not maintain a second eligibility registry for entity existence; the downstream entity owner validates that invariant.

Retained behavior: animation graphs are admitted through narrow catalog validation before service construction. Removed concept: incrementally registering generic gameplay machines in a second state store.

Retained behavior: an entity explicitly attaches one validated animation graph and receives its initial state. Removed concept: attaching an arbitrary generic ProcessId machine through a second entity registry.
Retained behavior: callers can read an entity's complete typed animation controller state. Removed concept: exposing a parallel generic MachineInstance state owner.
Retained behavior: controller ticks select validated edges and commit state atomically. Removed concept: callers submitting arbitrary generic transition requests to a second store.
Retained behavior: a valid transition updates current state and revision and emits a typed local transition fact. Removed concept: the replay-line representation asserted by the donor test.
Removed concept: the test covers only the bridge from generic machine state into Asha's global ProcessModeSet event.

Retained behavior: invalid animation graphs and failed controller input batches do not partially mutate live controller state. Removed concept: rejecting a caller-authored arbitrary next-state command at runtime.
Removed concept: stale expected-current checks belonged to the removed caller-authored generic transition command.
Removed concept: optimistic revision checks belonged to the removed caller-authored generic transition command.
Retained behavior: unknown graphs and missing controller instances return typed local errors. Removed concept: a second entity-eligibility registry plus global error-category classification.

Retained behavior: catalog admission rejects missing states and controller attachment rejects unknown graphs. Removed concept: accepting an arbitrary caller-selected next state for runtime validation.
Retained behavior: animation graph lookup and transition priority remain deterministic through ordered maps. Removed concept: public iteration over a separate generic state-machine specification.

Retained behavior: animation state transitions preserve validated edges and monotonically advancing revisions. Removed concept: a detached public transition primitive outside the responsible controller service.
Retained behavior: missing animation targets and clips fail locally with typed diagnostics. Removed concept: copying authority-origin proof envelopes into those diagnostics.

Retained behavior: an unavailable animation host degrades locally without presentation-to-gameplay callbacks. Removed concept: applying scene and presentation through one universal runtime frame facade.
Retained behavior: an unavailable audio host degrades locally with typed diagnostics. Removed concept: universal scene-plus-presentation application and copied authority-origin diagnostics.
Retained behavior: missing audio resources fail locally with typed resource diagnostics. Removed concept: copying authority-origin proof envelopes into those diagnostics.
Retained behavior: named optional presentation hosts are composed explicitly. Removed concept: a port bundle that also owns scene application for a universal runtime projection frame.
Retained behavior: presentation host application returns per-domain typed receipts. Removed concept: one runtime receipt carrying authority tick and scene-applied certification.

Retained behavior: ordered presentation operations dispatch to explicit domain hosts with isolated absence. Removed concept: one function validating and applying scene plus presentation as a universal runtime frame.

Retained behavior: renderer-neutral scene and presentation decoders validate their own versioned frames and contiguous operations. Removed concept: validation of a universal runtime composite, authority tick, and replay-scope marker.

Retained behavior: an unavailable billboard host degrades locally without disturbing other presentation domains. Removed concept: coupling that isolation proof to prior scene application through a universal runtime facade.
Retained behavior: the public host package exposes explicit surface and presentation-host composition. Removed concept: re-exporting the universal runtime-frame application facade.
Retained behavior: public renderer-neutral frame validation remains available from responsible packages. Removed concept: re-exporting universal runtime composite validation.
Retained behavior: callers can provide a named presentation host set. Removed concept: re-exporting a port type that also owns scene application for a universal runtime frame.
Retained behavior: callers receive typed presentation-domain application receipts. Removed concept: re-exporting a runtime receipt with authority tick and scene-applied certification.
